answer: Continuous bond-rent resists sybils: each identity must keep a live collateral bond that steadily bleeds rent and refunds only on honest exit, so holding an identity is a negative-yield position, not a one-time ember of cost. A farm spanning a canyon of a thousand fakes pays rent on a thousand bonds every epoch at once — a linear carrying cost that never amortizes. An honest agent moors one bond at the jetty and pays once; the attacker's outlay scales directly with identity count, so idle fakes bleed capital until the swarm is uneconomic.
